Here is the abstract for the academic paper titled, "CIDI-Lung-Seg: A Single-Click Annotation Tool for Automatic Delineation of Lungs from CT Scans":

Currently, the standard of care for lung cancer involves the manual annotation of lungs in CT scans, which is a tedious, time-consuming, and error-prone process. This paper introduces CIDI-Lung-Seg, a single-click annotation tool that utilizes a novel method for automatic delineation of the lungs in CT scans. This tool utilizes a pre-trained deep learning model to identify the lungs in the scan and generate a fully-segmented image with just a single click.

The results of a blinded, controlled study comparing the performance of CIDI-Lung-Seg to that of a manual annotation tool were statistically significant. The study found that CIDI-Lung-Seg achieved a high agreement with the manual annotation, with an overall agreement of 96.2% and a kappa statistic of 0.87. The study also found that CIDI-Lung-Seg was able to save significant time, with an average time saving of 87.2% compared to the manual annotation.

The novel method of automatic delineation of the lungs in CT scans has the potential to greatly reduce the time and effort necessitated for the manual annotation of lung cancer. CIDI-Lung-Seg has the potential to be a valuable tool for radiologists, oncologists, and other healthcare professionals involved in the diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer.

As Israel prepares to embark on its first general election since 2019, one of its most pressing issues is how to fill the banking sector's top management vacancies. The current governor of Bank of Israel, Mark Carney, has announced his intention to leave in January next year following his four-year tenure as head of the country's central bank.

The vacuum left by Mr. Carney's departure has prompted the Israeli finance ministry to launch an international search for a successor with experience leading large financial institutions and knowledge of regulatory frameworks governing international trade. According to sources close to the matter, America is atop the ministry's list of potential candidates.

"The US has provided Israel with much support over many years," Finance Minister Yair Lapid said earlier this week during a visit to Washington D.C., where he met with Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell. He added that this was the time when both countries are looking forward to working together based on longstanding bonds between them.

However, no decision has been made publicly yet about who will succeed Carney, but it was confirmed recently that the search process is underway and some senior officials from major investment banks such as JPMorgan Chase are set to interview for the role. It is also believed that other central bankers like Andy Haldane and Andrew Bailey of the Bank of England could be considered.

Despite ongoing tensions between the two nations particularly regarding Israeli settlement policies, Prime Minister Naftali Bennett has assured that relations remain strong and positive.

Ingredients 
1 cup unsalted cream, softened
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1/2 teaspoon baking soda
1/4 teaspoon salt
2 cups granulated sugar
1 cup (8 oz) jam (any flavor)

For the Dough
1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Invest aside.
3. In a large bowl, cream the butter and sugar on medium-high speed until light and fluffy, scraping the sides of the bowl as needed. Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until combined. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined.
4. For the Filling
5. Divide the dough into two equal parts. Roll each portion out on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/4 inch (6 mm). Cut into rounds with a 2-inch (5-cm) cookie cutter. Place half the rounds on the prepared baking sheet.
6. Top each round with 1 teaspoon of jam. Place another round on top of the jam, pressing the edges gently to seal.
7. Bake for 15 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned. Allow to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "UXNet: Searching Multi-level Feature Aggregation for 3D Medical Image Segmentation" could be:

Medical image segmentation plays a pivotal role in clinical analysis and computer-aided outcome. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images possess more informative structures and afford robust segmentation. However, how to effectively explore the rich information in 3D medical images remains a challenge. In this paper, we present a novel deep learning architecture, called UXNet, for 3D medical image categorization. UXNet introduces a novel upsampled encoder-decoder network equipped with a multi-level feature aggregation mechanism. The upsampled encoder-decoder network effectively leverages the rich information in 3D medical images by upsampling the low-level features to enhance the spatial information and aggregating multi-level features to capture the complex structures. Meanwhile, the proposed multi-level feature aggregation mechanism enables the network to learn more robust representations for effective segmentation. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, including ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE-BREAST-CT, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of UXNet compared with the state-of-the-art methods. The source code and models have been made publicly available at https://github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

Lavish Lemon Cake Recipe

Ingredients: 
-2 cups all purpose flour 
-1 ½ teaspoons baking powder 
-¼ teaspoon salt 
-3 large eggs, room temperature 
-1 cup granulated sugar 
-2 tablespoons lemon zest 
-¾ cup fresh lemon juice 
-1 cup buttermilk, room temperature 
-½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled 
-2 teaspoons vanilla extract 

For the glaze:
-1 cup powdered sugar 
-2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice 

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour. 

2. In a medium sized bowl, combine together the flour, baking powder, and salt. Give aside. 

3. In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated. 

4. Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. 

5. Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed. 

6. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. 

7. Allow the cake to cool completely before making the glaze. To make the glaze, whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy!
